messages.author: a5679449d442e116
messages.subject: Re: ggplot
parts:
In base R plotting functions (e.g. "plot", "points", "abline") there
is similar functionality as "hold on" in matlab -- you can build up a
plot layer by layer one command at a time by adding the parameter
"new=TRUE" to the command, which tells it not to wipe the graphics
device before drawing on it.

In ggplot2, I do not believe there is a supported way to force the
plotting to happen on top of drawing that is already present in the
graphics device. It _is_ possible to draw on top of a ggplot2 plot
using the base R plotting functions, but they almost certainly won't
do what you want them to do because the coordinate systems are
different.

However, ggplot2 does support multiple layer plots, it is just not
necessary to build them up one layer at a time (ggplot will draw over
the entire graphics device each time you evaluate a plot, but you can
add layers to the plot itself). If you have been using the "qplot"
function, you may want to move to using the "ggplot" call instead as
that makes it easier to understand the layers (although you can also
add layers on top of a plot generated with "qplot").

In ggplot2, you can add in (using the '+' sign!) as many layers as you
like to the plot. If you wish to check your work as you go, you can
give the plot object you are working on a name and add more layers to
it as you go. The one limitation is that the layers all have to be
using the same axes -- ggplot2 does not support drawing another set of
axes on top of a previous plot (such as to create subfigures),
although you can use faceting (facet_grid) with free scales if you
need to display data with different scales on the same plot (but they
won't be plotted over each other but rather as a separate plot below
or to the side).

For example:

> # you can create a ggplot plot that has no layers like this:
> p <- ggplot(data=mtcars)
> # if you evaluate this plot, it gives an error because there are no layers to be plotted - all it has is a connection to a data set
> p
Error: No layers in plot
> # now we can add a layer (lets say, of points)
> p <- p + geom_point(mapping=aes(x=mpg,y=wt,colour=disp))
> # now if we evaluate the plot, it will be displayed
> p
> # perhaps now we want to add some text to label the cars with gear=5
> mtcars.5spd <- subset(mtcars, subset=(gear==5))
> p <- p + geom_text(data=mtcars.5spd, mapping=aes(x=mpg,y=wt,label=rownames(mtcars.5spd)), colour="blue")
> p

This is probably the closest to what "hold on" does in MATLAB that you
can get with ggplot2. Does this answer your question?

Josh.

messages.author: 5a1b5a9591c118ef
messages.subject: Re: ggplot
parts:
You can overwrite grid.newpage(), which is the function responsible
for ggplot starting over with a new page every time,

grid.newpage <- function() message("ignoring you")
qplot(1,1)
last_plot() + theme_bw()
rm(grid.newpage)

alternatively, save ggplot as a grob and draw it,

p = qplot(1,1)
p2 = p + theme_bw()
g = ggplotGrob(p)
g2 = ggplotGrob(p2)
grid.draw(g)
grid.draw(g2)

None of these would be good ideas in practice, for obvious reasons.

baptiste
